To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of a ceramic packing with a large specific surface area (SAS) and a high porosity (P) leads to an increase of the liquid holdup in the column.

1) the hydrodynamic performance of ceramic packing elements can be significantly improved by changing the shape of the elements; 2) this is achieved by increasing the number of channels and the channel cross section, and by increasing the packing density and the channel length; 3) this leads to higher pressure drops, higher liquid retention and better mass transfer performance; 4) the hydrodynamics of the new packing elements is similar to the hydrodynamics in a bubble column, which means that the

(a) the hydrodynamical properties of packed columns depend on the column diameter, (b) the hydrodynamics of packed columns depend significantly on the particle size, and (c) the hydrodyanmics of packed columns depend strongly on the particle shape, but only for the smaller particles.
